bull_bear.body:
- Vertically integrated (spinning + weaving + sizing) reducing reliance on third-party yarn
- Located in Ahmedabad/Gujarat cotton belt with ready raw-material access
- High capacity utilisation (weaving 107% consol FY26, spinning 88.5%)
- Captive solar (rooftop + ground-mounted, ~10 MW aggregate) reducing power cost
- Experienced promoters (25+ years in textiles)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration — Top 10 customers = 70.33% of FY26 revenue, no firm long-term contracts
- Geographic concentration — ~97% of revenue from Gujarat
- Product concentration — Grey fabric ~96-97% of revenue
- Leverage / working-capital intensity — Consolidated borrowings Rs 1,777.61 mn, D/E 2.35x FY26; unsecured related-party loans Rs 324.37 mn repayable on demand
- Raw-material (cotton/yarn) price volatility — Cotton/yarn is the dominant input; margins exposed to price swings
- Regulatory/environmental compliance — Unit 2 operated without GPCB Consolidated Consent & Authorisation; delayed CS appointment; RoC filing discrepancies
- Promoter-related-party dealings — Land purchased from promoter/promoter-group at consideration below market value; personal guarantees by promoters

concerns_observed: Corporate guarantee of Rs 5,575 lakh (Rs 557.50 million) extended by the Company and Promoter Group company Alpine Weaving Pvt Ltd to secure subsidiary Alpine Cottweave LLP's Saraswat consortium facilities equals 76.49% of FY26 consolidated net worth of Rs 7,288.4 lakh; it may crystallise on any subsidiary default.

CRISIL downgraded the long-term rating from 'CRISIL BBB-/Stable' to 'CRISIL BB/Stable' and short-term from 'A3' to 'A4+' with an 'Issuer Not Cooperating' remark on June 15, 2026, following a fee dispute and the Company's request to withdraw CRISIL services.

Heavy dependence on government subsidies for reported profit: total subsidy (net SGST refund, electricity duty, interest subsidy) of Rs 1,096.8 / 359.7 / 502.3 lakh equalled 50.50% / 41.70% / 102.91% of PAT for FY26 / FY25 / FY24.
High leverage: total debt Rs 17,776.1 lakh against net worth Rs 7,288.4 lakh (D/E ~2.4x) with cash of only Rs 130.1 lakh at FY26; secured debt is floating-rate.

Customer concentration: top 10 customers were 71.86% / 70.19% / 70.33% of revenue and the single largest 13.64% / 8.77% / 16.09% (FY24/25/26), with no long-term commitments and correlated cluster credit risk.
Supplier concentration: top 10 suppliers were 81.43% / 82.76% / 64.26% of purchases and the top supplier up to 25.58%, without long-term supply contracts.

Related-party land acquisitions from Promoter/Director Sumit Champalal Agarwal and Promoter Group member Champalal Gopiram Agarwal aggregating Rs 786.4 lakh (Gangad Rs 360 lakh plus three Aslali parcels of Rs 29.3 / 155.3 / 241.8 lakh), each acquired below stated market value.
Concentrated single-product, single-state profile: Grey Fabric was 96.69% of FY26 revenue and Gujarat 97.37%; 100% domestic, leaving negligible product or geographic diversification.
Subsidiary dependence: Alpine Cottweave LLP contributed 35.89% of FY26 consolidated revenue and 38.58% of PAT (ex-NCI), concentrating consolidated results in one recently acquired entity.
Very high workforce churn: employee attrition 26.39% / 14.46% / 76.92% and KMP/SMP attrition 50.00% / 0.00% / 18.18% across FY24/25/26.
Unsecured related-party and other loans of Rs 3,243.7 lakh (consolidated, at 9-12% p.a.) are repayable on demand, a recall risk to liquidity.

Manufacturing Unit 2 commenced operations on March 28, 2025 before obtaining the GPCB Consolidated Consent and Authorization; the Company paid Rs 19.8 lakh regularisation and received CCA only on January 16, 2026.

Bonus issue of 7:1 (Dec 21, 2020) and two name changes in the run-up to filing (last on Feb 10, 2025); promoter average acquisition cost of Rs 1.99 / 2.52 / 8.01 per share is far below the intended issue price.

red_flags: Rs 5,575 lakh corporate guarantee for subsidiary Alpine Cottweave LLP equal to 76.49% of FY26 consolidated net worth (Rs 7,288.4 lakh) - an off-balance-sheet exposure that could crystallise on subsidiary default.
CRISIL downgrade to BB/Stable and A4+ with 'Issuer Not Cooperating' (June 15, 2026) following a fee dispute, while CARE separately rates BBB-/A3 - a two-notch split and a cooperation red flag.
Reported profit is subsidy-dependent: government subsidies were 50.50% / 41.70% / 102.91% of PAT for FY26/25/24, implying FY24 was loss-making before subsidies.

Related-party land acquisitions (Rs 786.4 lakh) below stated market value and below-market leases from Promoter/Promoter Group entities, alongside prior SEBI penalties on Promoter Group member Champalal Gopiram Agarwal.
Manufacturing Unit 2 ran before obtaining GPCB Consolidated Consent and Authorization, requiring a Rs 19.8 lakh regularisation - a compliance gap the DRHP flags could recur at Proposed Unit 3.
strengths_observed: Rapid top-line growth: consolidated revenue rose from Rs 18,360.3 lakh (FY24) to Rs 23,732.4 lakh (FY25) to Rs 34,271.3 lakh (FY26), roughly 37% two-year CAGR.
Margin expansion alongside scale: EBITDA margin improved from 10.84% (FY24) to 11.38% (FY25) to 13.84% (FY26); PAT margin from 2.66% to 6.34% over the same period.
Strong headline return ratios for FY26: ROE 33.85%, RONW 29.44%, ROCE 17.56%, up from ROE 12.17% / ROCE 12.12% in FY24.
High capacity utilisation of the weaving base: 95.41% (FY24), 106.51% (FY25) and 107.30% (FY26) on installed 276 lakh metres, indicating demand absorption of existing assets.

Backward integration executed: in-house spinning (Manufacturing Unit 2, commissioned Mar 2025, 88.5% utilisation FY26) plus acquisition of 97% of weaving subsidiary Alpine Cottweave LLP, reducing reliance on third-party yarn.
Captive solar lowered power intensity: power and fuel expense fell from 5.53% of revenue (FY24) to 4.30% (FY26) with 820 KW + 475 KW rooftop and 5.4 MW + 3.6 MW ground-mounted solar installed.
Deleveraging intent in the objects: Rs 5,220 lakh of fresh-issue proceeds earmarked to prepay/repay Saraswat and SVC bank cash-credit and term-loan facilities.

Largest single machinery order already placed: 48 Picanol NV air-jet looms (Rs 2,115.3 lakh, 89.54% of Unit 3 plant-and-machinery capex) contracted under LC, reducing part of the execution risk on the expansion.
